title: Globular Cluster NGC 1466
caption: The globular cluster NGC 1466, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Hubble reveals NGC 1466, an ancient, glimmering ball of stars. It is a globular cluster, a group of stars held together by gravity, moving slowly along the fringes of the Large Magellanic Cloud, a nearby neighbor galaxy.

NGC 1466 is a cluster of extremes. It holds a mass equal to roughly 140 000 Suns and is around 13.1 billion years old, almost as old as the Universe itself. That makes it something like a fossil left over from the early cosmos, preserving stars that formed very long ago.

Astronomers are interested in more than its age. NGC 1466 is one of five clusters in the Large Magellanic Cloud whose level of dynamical evolution has been measured. This so-called dynamical age describes how far the cluster's internal structure has changed as its stars interact gravitationally over time, which is different from simply how old its stars are.

understand.summary: The image combines ultraviolet data from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 with visible and near-infrared data from the Advanced Camera for Surveys. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Ultraviolet and near-infrared light are invisible to the eye, and Hubble resolves individual stars in another galaxy.
